title: Convert _scaled_grouped_mm_v2 to a structured operator
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #187357

Mirrors the recently-landed _scaled_mm_v2 work (#185271/#185272/#185273)
for the grouped sibling. The shared dispatch-table helper from that stack
already covers the grouped path, so this is the structured-op conversion
plus validation centralization.

Recipe-independent input validation (dim/contraction/divisibility/offsets/
bias/out_dtype) moves into a shared validate_scaled_grouped_mm_v2_inputs
helper called from the meta, so torch.compile tracing fails fast with the
same errors as eager. Per-recipe scale-shape checks and the device-capability
gate stay in the CUDA kernel, where they belong.

A thin Python meta is kept for shape inference only, since the structured C++
meta specializes symbolic dims and breaks mark_dynamic / unbacked symints
(same pattern as meta_mm and meta_scaled_mm_v2). The output size/stride math
is shared between it and the eager allocator.

Also gates test_mxfp8_nvfp4_scaled_grouped_mm_2d_2d and
test_mxfp8_scaled_grouped_mm_2d_3d with @onlyCUDA; a platform-global skip let
their CPU variants run and call the CUDA-only op, raising NotImplementedError.

Authored with assistance from Claude.

Test Plan:

CMAKE_FRESH=1 USE_CUDNN=1 USE_CUDA=1 USE_MSLK=1 \
    uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation

Run on a B200 (SM100):

python test/test_scaled_matmul_cuda.py TestFP8MatmulCUDA  # 914 pass
python test/test_scaled_matmul_cuda.py -k scaled_grouped  # 104 pass (27 run, 77 skip), 0 errors
python test/test_decomp.py HasDecompTest.test_has_decomposition
python test/test_meta.py -k scaled_mm
python test/test_flop_counter.py -k scaled_mm
python test/inductor/test_fp8.py
python test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py -k test_fp8

FP8 rowwise grouped (incl. test_scaled_grouped_mm_v2_fullgraph) is SM90-only
and skips on B200; the mxfp8/nvfp4/mxfp4 grouped 2d-2d and 2d-3d paths exercise
the structured kernel and pass. Dynamic-shape tracing (symbolic M through the
kept Python meta) verified via FakeTensorMode.
